title: Reflexive Descent to Minimal Seeds in the Kreuzer–Skarke List: code, data and checks
description:
Code, data and independent checks for the paper Reflexive Descent to Minimal Seeds in the Kreuzer–Skarke List by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya.

A reflexive polytope inside another is a cover when no reflexive polytope lies between them, and a reflexive descent is a chain of covers that ends at an r-minimal polytope. The paper proves that every reflexive polytope has such a descent and that it ends above a minimal seed; that in dimension four no descent has more than 348 steps, so that the conjecture of a uniform transition depth holds with D = 349; that the largest transition depths in dimensions two and three are 5 and 11; that two four-dimensional polytopes with 37 lattice points, skew bipyramids over a reflexive tetrahedron, have transition depth exactly 22, so that 22 ≤ D_4 ≤ 348; and that the largest four-dimensional polytope, the simplex with 680 lattice points, has transition depth at most 31; and that in every dimension d ≥ 4 a chain of reflexive polytopes has at most 2(s_d − 1)² − 2 steps, s_d being Sylvester's sequence, by Blichfeldt's bound on lattice points and the volume theorem of Balletti, Kasprzyk and Nill. The exact maximum in dimension four is open.

The archive holds the joint distribution of lattice point counts of the 473,800,776 four-dimensional reflexive polytopes and their duals, the pair bound with a longest chain, the cover relation of the 16 polygons and the 4,319 three-dimensional polytopes, the descent of the 680-point simplex with the certificate of every step, the certificate of depth 22 (5,592 polytopes with their complete lists of covers), the programs that computed them, and 87 independent checks: a C program for the pair bound, a C++ program for the 680-point simplex and its dual, Python checks of the pair bound, the descent, the three-dimensional depths, the depth-22 certificate, the cuts in dimension three and at the certificate, and the bound in every dimension, a Julia enumeration of the polygons from scratch, a Macaulay2 check with the Polyhedra package, and 27 Lean 4 theorems on the finite arithmetic, the counting lemma in dimension four and in every dimension, and the certificate lemma, each axiom-free or depending on propext only. code/run_checks.sh runs them all.
